page: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores placing the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. The AMD EPYC processor supports cryptographic and integer execution flags such as AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and ADX, which contribute to strong performance in PassMark encryption and extended instruction tests. Memory performance is mixed; small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is strong, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidth falls into the average category.

The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, as evidenced by top-tier Geekbench scores in these areas. It also performs well in database operations and Redis SET operations, making it suitable for high-throughput key-value stores and compute-heavy database tasks. For machine learning, the server achieves strong token generation speeds during LLM inference with smaller 135M models, though performance scales down to average levels for larger 7B and 70B models. This hardware profile offers a resource-dense compute configuration without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, making it a cost-efficient choice for CPU-bound workloads, batch processing, and distributed compilation.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.16xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results show strong CPU performance in stress-ng and PassMark tests, alongside strong capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. Conversely, large-block uncached memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput remain average. This configuration is well-suited for compute-intensive workloads, including software compilation, cryptographic processing, high-throughput database operations, and small-scale machine learning inference.
